qe: During the post-First World War years, the industrial sector in India faced an alarming crisis that fueled widespread anti-British sentiments. What was the nature of this economic hardship?
qh: प्रथम विश्व युद्ध के बाद के वर्षों में, भारत में औद्योगिक क्षेत्र को एक गंभीर संकट का सामना करना पड़ा जिसने व्यापक ब्रिटिश विरोधी भावनाओं को बढ़ावा दिया। इस आर्थिक तंगी की प्रकृति क्या थी?
o: A rise in commodity prices, coupled with a decrease in the production of Indian industries and an increase in taxes and rents
The complete, immediate state-enforced nationalization of all rural handicraft units
A sudden volumetric drop in the custom duty tariffs imposed on native sugar exports
The mandatory conversion of all corporate banks into non-profit cooperative societies
e: Detailed Explanation: Following the war, India suffered high inflation, an increased tax burden, a rise in commodity prices, and a production slump in domestic industries, creating a strong feeling of discontent across almost all sections of society.

qe: Which group of radical nationalist Muslim leaders became highly influential in the late 1910s, successfully steering the community toward militant nationalism and active participation in the freedom struggle?
qh: 1910 के दशक के उत्तरार्ध में कट्टरपंथी राष्ट्रवादी मुस्लिम नेताओं का कौन सा समूह अत्यधिक प्रभावशाली हो गया, जिसने समुदाय को जुझारू राष्ट्रवाद और स्वतंत्रता संग्राम में सक्रिय भागीदारी की ओर सफलतापूर्वक प्रेरित किया?
o: Mohammad Ali, Abul Kalam Azad, Hakim Ajmal Khan, and Hasan Imam
Sir Syed Ahmed Khan and the conservative elements of the Aligarh School
Mirza Ghulam Ahmad and the localized leaders of the Ahmadiyya sect
Haji Shariatullah and the paramilitary commanders of the Faraizi Front
e: Detailed Explanation: The political landscape shifted as younger, radical nationalist Muslim leaders—such as the Ali brothers, Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, Hakim Ajmal Khan, and Hasan Imam—outgrew the conservative Aligarh school to advocate anti-imperialist mass action.

qe: What dual demand did Indian Muslims present to the British government at the onset of the Khilafat agitation in early 1919 regarding the status of Turkey?
qh: भारतीय मुसलमानों ने 1919 की शुरुआत में खिलाफत आंदोलन की शुरुआत में तुर्की की स्थिति के संबंध में ब्रिटिश सरकार के सामने क्या दोहरी मांग रखी थी?
o: The Khalifa’s control over Muslim sacred places should be retained, and the Khalifa must be left with sufficient territories
The absolute permanent exile of the Sultan of Turkey to a non-Asian colonial territory
The immediate mandatory introduction of Western secular legal codes across all Islamic states
The total structural merging of the Ottoman caliphate with the British Commonwealth
e: Detailed Explanation: Following the dismemberment of Turkey after WWI, Indian Muslims demanded that the Khalifa (Sultan of Turkey) retain control over Islamic holy sites and be left with sufficient baseline territory to maintain his spiritual status.

qe: At the All India Khilafat Conference held in Delhi in November 1919, what significant program of political resistance was officially called for under the presidency of Mahatma Gandhi?
qh: नवंबर 1919 में दिल्ली में आयोजित अखिल भारतीय खिलाफत सम्मेलन में महात्मा गांधी की अध्यक्षता में राजनीतिक प्रतिरोध के किस महत्वपूर्ण कार्यक्रम का आधिकारिक आह्वान किया गया था?
o: A call for the boycott of British goods and a declaration to stop all cooperation if peace terms were unfavorable
An immediate armed parameter rebellion to seize the provincial legislative assemblies
A legal petition demanding the relocation of the Imperial Legislative Council to Constantinople
The mandatory implementation of English-medium technical education across all rural madrasas
e: Detailed Explanation: Presided over by Gandhi, the November 1919 Khilafat Conference issued a call to boycott British goods and declared that Muslims would stop all cooperation with the government if the post-war peace terms were unfavorable to Turkey.

qe: Why was the veteran leader Bal Gangadhar Tilak initially skeptical and opposed to forming an alliance with the Khilafat Committee over the Turkey question?
qh: दिग्गज नेता बाल गंगाधर तिलक शुरू में तुर्की के प्रश्न पर खिलाफत समिति के साथ गठबंधन करने के प्रति संशय में और विरोधी क्यों थे?
o: He was opposed to having a political alliance with Muslim leaders over a religious issue and was skeptical of satyagraha
He was legally barred by a decree of the Bombay High Court from interacting with Pan-Islamists
He firmly believed that the British Crown possessed a providential mission in resolving the caliphate
He aimed to restrict all anti-colonial mass agitations strictly to the city limits of Poona
e: Detailed Explanation: Tilak was initially conservative about linking the nationalist struggle with a religious issue like the Khilafat and doubted the political efficacy of Satyagraha, though Gandhi later convinced him of its strategic value to forge Hindu-Muslim unity.

qe: Apart from the golden opportunity to cement Hindu-Muslim unity, what internal development pushed the Indian National Congress to fully support the Non-Cooperation program by late 1820?
qh: हिंदू-मुस्लिम एकता को मजबूत करने के सुनहरे अवसर के अलावा, किस आंतरिक विकास ने भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस को 1920 के उत्तरार्ध तक असहयोग कार्यक्रम का पूर्ण समर्थन करने के लिए प्रेरित किया?
o: The Congress was rapidly losing faith in constitutional struggle after the Punjab atrocities and the blatantly partisan Hunter Report
The colonial administration offered complete provincial autonomy to popular ministries under Dyarchy
The sudden, absolute liquidation of all agrarian peasant debts by a state decree
The direct financial funding provided by the British Cabinet to support the setting up of national schools
e: Detailed Explanation: The Congress lost faith in British justice and constitutional methods due to the government's harsh actions in Punjab and the highly partisan 'whitewashing' report of the Hunter Committee, which led them to adopt extra-constitutional mass struggle.

qe: The peace treaty signed in May 1920 that completely dismembered the Ottoman Empire and finalized the removal of the Khalifa, triggering intense anger among Indian Muslims, was:
qh: मई 1920 में हस्ताक्षरित वह शांति संधि जिसने ओटोमन साम्राज्य को पूरी तरह से विभाजित कर दिया और खलीफा को हटाने को अंतिम रूप दिया, जिससे भारतीय मुसलमानों में तीव्र आक्रोश फैल गया, कौन सी थी?
o: The Treaty of Sevres
The Treaty of Versailles
The Treaty of Sagauli
The Paris Peace Accord
e: Detailed Explanation: The Treaty of Sevres, signed in May 1920 between the Allied powers and Turkey, completely dismembered the Ottoman Empire, directly validating the worst fears of the Khilafat movement.

qe: An all-party conference convened at Allahabad in June 1920 approved a comprehensive boycott program. What critical leadership decision was taken during this conference?
qh: जून 1920 में इलाहाबाद में आयोजित एक सर्वदलीय सम्मेलन (all-party conference) ने एक व्यापक बहिष्कार कार्यक्रम को मंजूरी दी। इस सम्मेलन के दौरान नेतृत्व का कौन सा महत्वपूर्ण निर्णय लिया गया था?
o: The conference formally asked Mahatma Gandhi to lead the Non-Cooperation movement
They elected Mohammad Ali Jinnah as the permanent chairman of the Congress Working Committee
It was decided to completely suspend any active boycott of colonial law courts and schools
They moved the organizational headquarters of the Satyagraha Sabha to the Madras Presidency
e: Detailed Explanation: The June 1920 all-party meeting in Allahabad adopted the program of boycotting schools, colleges, and courts, and formally requested Mahatma Gandhi to take over the leadership of the movement.

qe: On August 31, 1920, the Khilafat Committee officially launched its non-cooperation campaign. Which iconic Indian nationalist leader passed away on the same day the movement was set in motion?
qh: 31 अगस्त, 1920 को खिलाफत समिति ने आधिकारिक तौर पर अपना असहयोग अभियान शुरू किया। आंदोलन शुरू होने के ठीक उसी दिन किस प्रतिष्ठित भारतीय राष्ट्रवादी नेता का निधन हो गया था?
o: Bal Gangadhar Tilak
Gopal Krishna Gokhale
Pherozshah Mehta
Ananda Mohan Bose
e: Detailed Explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak passed away on August 1, 1920, just as the campaign was gathering steam, and his death was marked by nationwide grief on August 31, 1920, the day the Non-Cooperation movement was formally launched.

qe: At a special Congress session hosted in Calcutta in September 1920, a programmatic charter for non-cooperation was approved. Which of the following fields was included in this initial boycott strategy?
qh: सितंबर 1920 में कलकत्ता में आयोजित एक विशेष कांग्रेस सत्र में असहयोग के लिए एक कार्यक्रम संबंधी चार्टर को मंजूरी दी गई थी। इस प्रारंभिक बहिष्कार रणनीति में निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा क्षेत्र शामिल था?
o: Boycott of government schools, colleges, law courts, legislative councils, and foreign cloth
The immediate armed picketing of all local village panchayat arbitration courts
The total structural non-cooperation with native khadi hand-spinning setups
Mandatory resignation of all low-caste peasants from their ancestral agrarian lands
e: Detailed Explanation: The Calcutta special session approved a non-cooperation plan that included boycotting government educational institutions, law courts (replacing them with panchayats), legislative councils, and foreign cloth while promoting Khadi.

qe: The landmark Nagpur session of the Indian National Congress in December 1920 introduced a profound shift in the 'Congress creed'. What was this fundamental constitutional change?
qh: दिसंबर 1920 में भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस के ऐतिहासिक नागपुर सत्र ने 'कांग्रेस पंथ' (Congress creed) में एक गहरा बदलाव पेश किया। यह मौलिक संवैधानिक परिवर्तन क्या था?
o: Shifting its goal from attaining self-government through constitutional means to attaining swaraj through peaceful and legitimate means, committing to an extra-constitutional mass struggle
Declaring an immediate absolute armed separation from the British Commonwealth frame permanently
Restricting its political membership parameters strictly to the English-educated intellectual elite
The total structural dissolution of any central or provincial working committees
e: Detailed Explanation: At Nagpur, the Congress altered its constitutional creed: it moved away from seeking self-government through legal, constitutional methods to aiming for Swaraj through peaceful and legitimate means, officially embracing extra-constitutional mass struggle.

qe: To manage the expanding, continuous operations of the national movement on a daily basis, what specific executive body of 15 members was set up for the first time during the 1920 Nagpur session?
qh: दैनिक आधार पर राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन के विस्तारित कार्यों को प्रबंधित करने के लिए, 1920 के नागपुर सत्र के दौरान पहली बार 15 सदस्यों के किस विशिष्ट कार्यकारी निकाय का गठन किया गया था?
o: The Congress Working Committee (CWC)
The Satyagraha Executive Council
The All India Khilafat High Command
The Central Legislative Advisory Board
e: Detailed Explanation: The Nagpur session introduced major organizational reforms. It created a 15-member Congress Working Committee (CWC) to provide continuous executive leadership, set up Provincial Congress Committees on a linguistic basis, and reduced the entry fee to 4 annas.

qe: Which prominent political figures formally broke away and left the Indian National Congress after the 1920 Nagpur session because they firmly opposed extra-constitutional mass struggles and believed strictly in a constitutional, lawful fight?
qh: 1920 के नागपुर सत्र के बाद कौन से प्रमुख राजनीतिक व्यक्ति औपचारिक रूप से अलग हो गए और भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस छोड़ दी क्योंकि वे असंवैधानिक जन संघर्षों के सख्त खिलाफ थे और केवल संवैधानिक लड़ाई में विश्वास करते थे?
o: Mohammad Ali Jinnah, Annie Besant, G.S. Khaparde, and B.C. Pal
Motilal Nehru, Jawaharlal Nehru, and C.R. Das
Lala Lajpat Rai, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, and Rajendra Prasad
Subhash Chandra Bose, Acharya Narendra Dev, and Zakir Hussain
e: Detailed Explanation: Leaders like Mohammad Ali Jinnah, Annie Besant, G.S. Khaparde, and B.C. Pal chose to leave the Congress at this stage because they were committed to legal, constitutional methods and opposed the newly adopted extra-constitutional mass non-cooperation program.

qe: During the spread of the movement, thousands of students left government colleges. Which dynamic young nationalist leader was appointed as the Principal of the newly established National College at Calcutta?
qh: आंदोलन के प्रसार के दौरान हजारों छात्रों ने सरकारी कॉलेज छोड़ दिए। कलकत्ता में नव स्थापित नेशनल कॉलेज के प्राचार्य के रूप में किस गतिशील युवा राष्ट्रवादी नेता को नियुक्त किया गया था?
o: Subhash Chandra Bose
Acharya Narendra Dev
Zakir Hussain
C.R. Das
e: Detailed Explanation: Hundreds of national schools and colleges were set up to accommodate students who boycotted government institutions. Subhash Chandra Bose left his civil services prospects and was appointed as the Principal of the National College at Calcutta.

qe: The financial backbone of the Non-Cooperation Movement was secured through a commemorative national fund that was oversubscribed to collect more than one crore rupees. What was the name of this fund?
qh: असहयोग आंदोलन की वित्तीय रीढ़ को एक स्मारक राष्ट्रीय कोष (national fund) के माध्यम से सुरक्षित किया गया था, जिसमें एक करोड़ रुपये से अधिक एकत्र किए गए थे। इस फंड का नाम क्या था?
o: The Tilak Swaraj Fund
The Dayal Singh Trust Fund
The Gandhi Satyagraha Capital
The Harijan Upliftment Pool
e: Detailed Explanation: To finance the nationwide anti-colonial agitations and constructive works, the leadership launched the Tilak Swaraj Fund, which was enthusiastically oversubscribed by the public, collecting over 1 crore rupees within a short period.

qe: In July 1921, the Ali brothers issued a powerful religious decree to Muslim soldiers serving under the British Raj. What did this resolution call for, leading to their subsequent arrest in September?
qh: जुलाई 1921 में, अली भाइयों ने ब्रिटिश राज के तहत सेवा कर रहे मुस्लिम सैनिकों के लिए एक शक्तिशाली धार्मिक फरमान जारी किया। इस प्रस्ताव में क्या आह्वान किया गया था, जिसके कारण सितंबर में उनकी गिरफ्तारी हुई?
o: A call to all Muslims to resign from the British Army as it was unreligious
A demand to immediately transfer all frontline troops to the Ottoman caliphate borders
An instruction to strictly collect manual land taxes from local lower-caste ryots
A mandate forcing soldiers to exclusively wear foreign manufactured cloth uniforms
e: Detailed Explanation: At the Karachi Khilafat conference in July 1921, the Ali brothers declared it religiously unlawful for Muslims to serve in the British Army. They were arrested for this in September, after which Gandhi and the Congress duplicated the resolution across local committees.

qe: During the dynamic expansion of the movement, localized agrarian tax revolts erupted independently. A prominent 'no-tax movement' against union board taxes was organized in which two regions?
qh: आंदोलन के गतिशील विस्तार के दौरान, स्थानीय स्तर पर कृषि कर विद्रोह स्वतंत्र रूप से भड़क उठे। यूनियन बोर्ड करों के खिलाफ एक प्रमुख 'नो-टैक्स आंदोलन' (no-tax movement) किन दो क्षेत्रों में आयोजित किया गया था?
o: Midnapore in Bengal and Guntur in Andhra
Champaran in Bihar and Kheda in Gujarat
Gorakhpur in United Provinces and Malabar in Kerala
Tuticorin in Madras and Rawalpindi in Punjab Plain
e: Detailed Explanation: The non-cooperation spirit triggered local grievances. Peasant-driven 'no-tax' campaigns against local union board taxes broke out autonomously in Midnapore (Bengal) and Guntur (Andhra).

qe: In Assam, the nationalist upsurge triggered major industrial strikes across tea plantations and transport lines. Which prominent leader successfully organized these strikes in the Assam-Bengal Railways and steamer services?
qh: असम में, राष्ट्रवादी उभार ने चाय बागानों और परिवहन लाइनों में बड़े पैमाने पर औद्योगिक हड़तालें शुरू कीं। असम-बंगाल रेलवे और स्टीमर सेवाओं में इन हड़तालों को किस प्रमुख नेता ने सफलतापूर्वक आयोजित किया था?
o: J.M. Sengupta
Subhash Chandra Bose
C.R. Das
Ashwini Kumar Dutta
e: Detailed Explanation: Labor unrest became an integral aspect of anti-colonial resistance. In Assam, strikes in tea plantations, river steamer services, and the Assam-Bengal Railways were powerfully led and coordinated by J.M. Sengupta.

qe: The arrival of which high-profile British royal figure to India in November 1921 was greeted with unprecedented nationwide strikes, closure of markets, and massive hostile demonstrations?
qh: नवंबर 1921 में किस हाई-प्रोफाइल ब्रिटिश शाही व्यक्ति के भारत आगमन पर अभूतपूर्व देशव्यापी हड़ताल, बाजारों के बंद होने और बड़े पैमाने पर उग्र प्रदर्शनों के साथ स्वागत किया गया था?
o: The Prince of Wales
Lord William Hunter
The Duke of Connaught
King George V
e: Detailed Explanation: When the Prince of Wales visited India in November 1921, the Congress organized a complete boycott of his tour, greeting his arrival in Bombay and other cities with empty streets, general strikes (hartals), and massive demonstrations.

qe: The widespread spirit of anti-colonial defiance gave rise to several intense local struggles across India. Which of the following agrarian rebellions erupted during this phase within the Malabar region of Kerala?
qh: अपनिवेशिक अवज्ञा की व्यापक भावना ने भारत भर में कई तीव्र स्थानीय संघर्षों को जन्म दिया। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा कृषि विद्रोह केरल के मालाबार क्षेत्र के भीतर इस चरण के दौरान भड़का था?
o: Mappila Revolt
Awadh Kisan Movement
Eka Movement
Sikh Akali Agitation
e: Detailed Explanation: The popular non-cooperation landscape triggered localized peasant rebellions against oppressive landlords and state revenue systems, most notably the intense Mappila Revolt (or Moplah Uprising) in the Malabar district of Kerala.

qe: When evaluating the response of different social classes, why did the educated urban middle class elite show reservations and a limited response to Gandhi's call in major presidency centers like Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras?
qh: विभिन्न सामाजिक वर्गों की प्रतिक्रिया का मूल्यांकन करते समय, कलकत्ता, बॉम्बे और मद्रास जैसे प्रमुख प्रेसीडेंसी केंद्रों में शिक्षित शहरी मध्यम वर्ग के अभिजात वर्ग ने गांधी के आह्वान के प्रति आरक्षण और सीमित प्रतिक्रिया क्यों दिखाई?
o: These presidency centers were the traditional strongholds of elite politicians who preferred constitutional legal methods over mass agitations
They were legally barred from resigning from government services by an absolute decree of the Federal Court
They suffered from a total lack of financial capital investments following the Treaty of Sevres
They were entirely composed of orthodox groups belonging to the conservative Dharma Sabha
e: Detailed Explanation: In the traditional political centers of Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras, the older elite politicians showed hesitation toward Gandhi's mass lines. They did not take the call to surrender titles or resign from government posts seriously, leaving leadership to newer elements in Indian politics.

qe: Why did the domestic Indian business and industrial groups actively extend their support to the economic boycott program during the Non-Cooperation Movement?
qh: असहयोग आंदोलन के दौरान घरेलू भारतीय व्यापारिक और औद्योगिक समूहों ने आर्थिक बहिष्कार कार्यक्रम को अपना सक्रिय समर्थन क्यों दिया?
o: They directly benefited from the nationalists' systematic emphasis on the use of Swadeshi and the drop in foreign imports
The colonial administration offered them flat financial subsidies to completely close their factories
They aimed to entirely eliminate their internal dependency on the labor unions and kisan sabhas
The Treaty of Sevres legally granted them a monopoly over all maritime trade routes heading to Europe
e: Detailed Explanation: Indian industrial and mercantile classes supported the economic boycott of foreign goods because the nationalist focus on Swadeshi and the public burning of imported textiles cut imports by half, directly expanding the domestic market for Indian-manufactured goods.

qe: During the peasant mobilizations in Bihar, a localized social confrontation between lower and upper castes over a specific ritual right became completely merged with the Non-Cooperation Movement. What was this issue?
qh: बिहार में किसान लामबंदी के दौरान, एक विशिष्ट अनुष्ठानिक अधिकार को लेकर निचली और ऊंची जातियों के बीच एक स्थानीय सामाजिक टकराव पूरी तरह से असहयोग आंदोलन में विलय हो गया। यह मुद्दा क्या था?
o: The right of lower castes to wear the sacred thread (janeyu)
The access of untouchables to draw water from the public Chawdar tank
The compulsory registration of lower-caste births inside municipal district boards
The right of non-Brahmin intermediate castes to study original Sanskrit scriptures
e: Detailed Explanation: In Bihar, the anti-colonial mass surge integrated deep social dynamics. A localized movement where lower castes asserted social equality by donning the sacred thread (traditionally restricted to upper castes) merged with the broader political non-cooperation campaign.

qe: How did the participating Indian women register their historic mass mobilization and support for the movement after breaking away from the traditional constraints of the purdah system?
qh: पारंपरिक पर्दा प्रथा की बाधाओं को तोड़ने के बाद भाग लेने वाली भारतीय महिलाओं ने आंदोलन के लिए अपनी ऐतिहासिक जन लामबंदी और समर्थन कैसे दर्ज किया?
o: They offered their personal ornaments for the Tilak Fund and actively participated in the picketing of foreign cloth and liquor shops
They filed thousands of joint civil lawsuits inside the local high court rooms against the bureaucracy
They organized alternative maritime shipping lines to transport raw cotton to Japan independently
They surrenedered their property inheritance rights to the local Provincial Congress Committees
e: Detailed Explanation: Women stepped into public activism on an unprecedented scale during this movement. They discarded the purdah system, donated their gold ornaments to the Tilak Swaraj Fund, and stood at the front lines picketing shops that sold foreign cloth or liquor.

qe: What extraordinary inter-communal phenomenon marked the mass mobilization of the Non-Cooperation Khilafat movement, which was unique in the history of the freedom struggle?
qh: असहयोग खिलाफत आंदोलन की जन लामबंदी की विशेषता कौन सी असाधारण अंतर-सामप्रदायिक परिघटना थी, जो स्वतंत्रता संग्राम के इतिहास में अद्वितीय थी?
o: Unprecedented Hindu-Muslim unity where massive numbers of Muslims participated, and Gandhi addressed crowds from inside mosques
The complete administrative merger of the Indian National Congress and the orthodox Hindu Dharma Sabha
A total structural reconciliation between the conservative Aligarh school and the Deoband school ulema
The mandatory selection of all legislative council members via an open multi-communal examination system
e: Detailed Explanation: The movement achieved a historic level of Hindu-Muslim unity. Massive numbers of Muslims participated (frequently forming two-thirds of those arrested), and Gandhi and other Hindu leaders were invited to address mixed or female Muslim gatherings from inside mosques.

qe: In May 1921, peace talks between Mahatma Gandhi and the Viceroy, Lord Reading, broke down due to a specific demand made by the colonial government. What was this demand?
qh: मई 1921 में, महात्मा गांधी और वायसराय लॉर्ड रीडिंग के बीच शांति वार्ता औपनिवेशिक सरकार द्वारा की गई एक विशिष्ट मांग के कारण टूट गई। यह मांग क्या थी?
o: The government wanted Gandhi to urge the Ali brothers to remove those portions from their speeches which suggested violence
The Viceroy demanded the immediate and complete dissolution of the newly formed Congress Working Committee
The state required Gandhi to pay a flat corporate tax surcharge derived from the Tilak Swaraj Fund savings
The British Cabinet forced the immediate legal deportation of all striking railwaymen union leaders
e: Detailed Explanation: Lord Reading's government tried to drive a wedge between Gandhi and the Khilafat leaders by asking Gandhi to publicly urge the Ali brothers to retract statements that allegedly suggested violence. Realizing the trap to split the movement's unity, Gandhi refused, leading to a breakdown of talks.

qe: During the intense crackdowns by the colonial state in December 1921, what specific administrative step was taken to legally paralyze the nationalist volunteers?
qh: दिसंबर 1921 में औपनिवेशिक राज्य द्वारा किए गए कड़े दमन के दौरान, राष्ट्रवादी स्वयंसेवकों को कानूनी रूप से पंगु बनाने के लिए कौन सा विशिष्ट प्रशासनिक कदम उठाया गया था?
o: The government declared all nationalist volunteer corps illegal, banned public meetings, and gagged the press
The state passed a summary decree nationalizing all private property assets held by the Kashi Vidyapeeth
The administration completely abolished the separate中央 and provincial administrative subject lists
The judiciary forced all arrested political workers to undergo manual labor inside the local arsenal workshops
e: Detailed Explanation: As the agitations became unmanageable by late 1921, the government resorted to fierce repression. They outlawed all Congress and Khilafat volunteer corps, banned public assemblies, imposed strict controls on the press, and jailed thousands of activists.

qe: The Ahmedabad session of the Indian National Congress in 1921 appointed Mahatma Gandhi as the sole authority on starting civil disobedience. Who was the elected President of this session who had to remain absent because he was in jail?
qh: 1921 में भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस के अहमदाबाद सत्र ने महात्मा गांधी को सविनय अवज्ञा शुरू करने का एकमात्र अधिकार नियुक्त किया। इस सत्र के निर्वाचित अध्यक्ष कौन थे जिन्हें जेल में होने के कारण अनुपस्थित रहना पड़ा था?
o: C.R. Das
Hakim Ajmal Khan
Motilal Nehru
Lala Lajpat Rai
e: Detailed Explanation: Chittaranjan Das (C.R. Das) was elected to preside over the 1921 Ahmedabad session. Since he was imprisoned during the December crackdown, Hakim Ajmal Khan acted as the session's temporary president.

qe: On February 1, 1922, Mahatma Gandhi sent an ultimatum to the Viceroy threatening to launch a mass civil disobedience campaign from which location if political prisoners were not released?
qh: 1本 फरवरी, 1922 को महात्मा गांधी ने वायसराय को एक अल्टीमेटम भेजा, जिसमें धमकी दी गई थी कि यदि राजनीतिक कैदियों को रिहा नहीं किया गया तो वे किस स्थान से सामूहिक सविनय अवज्ञा आंदोलन शुरू करेंगे?
o: Bardoli (Gujarat)
Chauri Chaura (UP)
Midnapore (Bengal)
Guntur (Andhra)
e: Detailed Explanation: Gandhi issued an ultimatum to Lord Reading on February 1, 1922, declaring his intention to launch a massive civil disobedience and no-tax campaign from Bardoli in Gujarat unless the government released political prisoners and lifted controls on the press.

qe: What violent event occurred on February 5, 1922, in a village within the Gorakhpur district of the United Provinces, prompting Gandhi to abruptly suspend the entire national movement?
qh: संयुक्त प्रांत के गोरखपुर जिले के एक गाँव में 5 फरवरी, 1922 को कौन सी हिंसक घटना घटी, जिसने गांधी को अचानक पूरे राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन को स्थगित करने के लिए प्रेरित किया?
o: The Chauri Chaura incident
The Vaikom Sataygraha clash
The Mahad tank riot
The Muzaffarpur bomb out-break
e: Detailed Explanation: On February 5, 1922, at Chauri Chaura, an agitated crowd, provoked by police firing, set fire to the local police station, resulting in the death of 22 policemen. Committed to strict non-violence, Gandhi decided to halt the movement immediately.

qe: Following the Chauri Chaura violence, the Congress Working Committee formally met to ratify the withdrawal of the movement and redirect cadres toward constructive village work. Where did this historic meeting take place in February 1922?
qh: चौरी चौरा हिंसा के बाद, कांग्रेस कार्य समिति ने औपचारिक रूप से आंदोलन को वापस लेने की पुष्टि करने और कार्यकर्ताओं को रचनात्मक ग्रामीण कार्यों की ओर मोड़ने के लिए बैठक की। फरवरी 1922 में यह ऐतिहासिक बैठक कहाँ हुई थी?
o: Bardoli
Calcutta
Nagpur
Allahabad
e: Detailed Explanation: The Congress Working Committee met at Bardoli (Gujarat) in February 1922. They passed resolutions to call off the law-breaking agitations and focused instead on constructive tasks like promoting Khadi, setting up national schools, and fighting untouchability.

qe: Which young leader voiced deep nationalist resentment by describing the sudden order of retreat—just when public enthusiasm was reaching a boiling point—as nothing short of a 'national calamity'?
qh: किस युवा नेता ने सार्वजनिक उत्साह के ठीक उबलते बिंदु पर पहुंचने पर अचानक पीछे हटने के आदेश को एक 'राष्ट्रीय आपदा' (national calamity) कहकर गहरा राष्ट्रवादी आक्रोश व्यक्त किया था?
o: Subhas Chandra Bose
Jawaharlal Nehru
C.R. Das
Lala Lajpat Rai
e: Detailed Explanation: Gandhi's sudden withdrawal of the movement created widespread bewilderment and resentment among front-line leaders. In his later reflections, Subhas Chandra Bose labeled the abrupt retreat at the movement's peak as a national calamity.

qe: In March 1922, Mahatma Gandhi was arrested and sentenced to six years in jail. What memorable stance did he articulate during his historic court speech before the judge?
qh: मार्च 1922 में, महात्मा गांधी को गिरफ्तार किया गया और छह साल की जेल की सजा सुनाई गई। उन्होंने न्यायाधीश के सामने अपने ऐतिहासिक अदालती भाषण के दौरान क्या यादगार रुख व्यक्त किया था?
o: He invited and submitted cheerfully to the highest penalty for what in law was a deliberate crime but appeared to him as the highest duty of a citizen
He filed an immediate request for absolute legal immunity under the guidelines of the British Indemnity Act
He completely blamed the ulema of the Khilafat Committee for provoking the violence at Chauri Chaura
He demanded that his trial must be conducted strictly under the supervision of the newly formed Federal Court
e: Detailed Explanation: During his famous trial in March 1922, Gandhi maintained his moral stance, stating that he cheerfully invited the highest penalty for what the state categorized as a crime, but what he considered his primary moral duty as a citizen resisting an unjust rule.

qe: A logistical coordinate grid maps an exact right-angled triangular course from central node O. A survey vehicle moves 12 km North, and then shifts orientation to move 5 km East to reach target research spot T. Find the straight-line distance from O to T.
qh: एक कार डिपो O से 12 किमी उत्तर की ओर चलती है, और फिर दिशा बदलकर पूर्व की ओर 5 किमी जाकर गंतव्य T पर पहुँचती है। O से T की सीधी रेखा की दूरी ज्ञात कीजिए।
o: 13 km
17 km
15 km
14 km
e:
Detailed Explanation: This spatial movement sets up a right-angled triangle with perpendicular legs of 12 km and 5 km. The direct straight-line distance is the hypotenuse.
By applying the Pythagoras theorem: $\text{Distance} = \sqrt{12^2 + 5^2} = \sqrt{144 + 25} = \sqrt{169} = \mathbf{13\text{ km}}$.

qe: In a biological survey tracking ecosystem energy parameters, if the Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) of an alluvial marsh plain is 38,000 units and the energy lost during plant respiration (R) is 18,000 units, calculate the Net Primary Productivity (NPP).
qh: ऊर्जा मापदंडों का मानचित्रण करने वाले एक पारिस्थितिकी उत्पादकता सर्वेक्षण में, यदि सकल प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (GPP) 38,000 इकाइयाँ है और पौधों के श्वसन (R) के दौरान खर्च की गई ऊर्जा 18,000 इकाइयाँ है, तो शुद्ध प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (NPP) की गणना करें।
o: 20,000 units
56,000 units
18,000 units
16,000 units
e:
Detailed Explanation: Utilizing the foundational ecological productivity balance formula: $NPP = GPP - R$.
Substituting the values: $NPP = 38,000 - 18,000 = \mathbf{20,000\text{ units}}$.

qe: What structural feature distinguished the newly modified goal of the Indian National Congress passed at the December 1920 Nagpur session from its older traditional political constitutional base?
qh: दिसंबर 1920 के नागपुर सत्र में पारित भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस के नए संशोधित लक्ष्य को उसके पुराने पारंपरिक राजनीतिक संवैधानिक आधार से कौन सी संरचनात्मक विशेषता अलग करती थी?
o: It committed the Congress to an extra-constitutional mass struggle aimed at attaining Swaraj through peaceful and legitimate means
It restricted the scope of all active boycott agitations strictly to the presidency capital cities
It required all future national resolutions to be validated by the British Chamber of Commerce in London
It completely abandoned any political propaganda or educational campaigns across rural areas
e: Detailed Explanation: The Nagpur session of December 1920 changed the Congress creed from seeking self-government through strictly legal, constitutional methods to aiming for Swaraj through peaceful and legitimate means, officially committing the organization to extra-constitutional mass struggle.

qe: The Marxist interpretation of the Non-Cooperation Movement argues that the popular groundswell of labor and peasant unrest in 1919-20 forced the leadership to a radical posture. According to this critique, why did the leadership call off the movement?
qh: असहयोग आंदोलन की मार्क्सवादी व्याख्या का तर्क है कि 1919-20 में मजदूर और किसान अशांति के लोकप्रिय उभार ने नेतृत्व को एक कट्टरपंथी रुख अपनाने के लिए मजबूर किया। इस आलोचना के अनुसार, नेतृत्व ने आंदोलन को क्यों वापस लिया?
o: To keep the revolutionary mass movement a 'controlled' affair and 'within safe channels' just when the masses seemed to be taking the initiative
Because the colonial administration successfully fulfilled 100% of the joint constitutional demands of the Lucknow Pact
Because the working-class populations completely refused to support the boycott of foreign cloth and liquor
To allow the permanent implementation of the rowlatt act guidelines without any further public hindrances
e: Detailed Explanation: The Marxist critique suggests that the elite leadership feared losing control over the spontaneous revolutionary energy of the workers and peasants. They argue the movement was intentionally suspended to keep it within 'safe channels' just as the masses were beginning to take independent initiative.

qe: What progressive organizational adjustment was made to the local tier of the Congress framework during the 1920 Nagpur session to make it structurally more accessible and representative of the language divisions of India?
qh: 1920 के नागपुर सत्र के दौरान कांग्रेस ढांचे के स्थानीय स्तर पर कौन सा प्रगतिशील संगठनात्मक समायोजन किया गया था ताकि इसे संरचनात्मक रूप से अधिक सुलभ और भारत के भाषाई विभाजनों का प्रतिनिधि बनाया जा सके?
o: The organization of Provincial Congress Committees on a linguistic basis
The mandatory restriction of membership exclusively to English-medium barristers
The complete administrative abolition of all village and ward level committees
The direct financial subordination of the Congress Working Committee to local zamindars
e: Detailed Explanation: To transform the Congress into a true mass organization, the Nagpur session reorganized Provincial Congress Committees on a linguistic basis rather than following British administrative lines, while setting up local ward committees and lowering the entry fee to 4 annas.

qe: During the nationwide student boycotts, several prominent national educational institutions cropped up to offer alternative learning options under national control. Which of the following universities was newly established or expanded during this phase?
qh: देशव्यापी छात्र बहिष्कारों के दौरान, राष्ट्रीय नियंत्रण के तहत वैकल्पिक शिक्षण विकल्प प्रदान करने के लिए कई प्रमुख राष्ट्रीय शैक्षणिक संस्थान सामने आए। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा विश्वविद्यालय इस चरण के दौरान नव स्थापित या विस्तारित किया गया था?
o: Jamia Millia at Aligarh, Kashi Vidyapeeth, Gujarat Vidyapeeth, and Bihar Vidyapeeth
Dayal Singh College at Lahore and Central Hindu College at Benaras exclusively
The Sanskrit College of Calcutta and the Royal Observatory infrastructure
The Bombay Presidency Academic Center and the Fergusson College campus
e: Detailed Explanation: The non-cooperation educational movement led to the creation of several pioneering national universities managed by prominent intellectuals, including Jamia Millia Islamia (initially at Aligarh), Kashi Vidyapeeth, Gujarat Vidyapeeth, and Bihar Vidyapeeth.

qe: Which of the following pairs correctly matches the prominent independent nationalist leader who gave up his lucrative legal practice with his respective region during the spread of the Non-Cooperation Movement?
qh: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा जोड़ा उस प्रमुख स्वतंत्र राष्ट्रवादी नेता का सही मिलान करता है जिसने असहयोग आंदोलन के प्रसार के दौरान अपने संबंधित क्षेत्र के साथ अपनी आकर्षक कानूनी प्रैक्टिस छोड़ दी थी?
o: Rajendra Prasad — Bihar, and Vallabhbhai Patel — Gujarat
Motilal Nehru — Madras Presidency, and T. Prakasam — Bengal delta
C. Rajagopalachari — Punjab plains, and Saifuddin Kitchlew — Bombay city
Asaf Ali — Assam tea plantations, and C.R. Das — United Provinces
e: Detailed Explanation: During the movement, leading lawyers abandoned their practices to join the struggle. This included Rajendra Prasad in Bihar, Vallabhbhai Patel in Gujarat, Motilal and Jawaharlal Nehru in the United Provinces, C.R. Das in Bengal, and C. Rajagopalachari in Madras.

qe: What significant change occurred in the physical import data parameters of foreign cloth textiles into India as a direct consequence of the public burning and Swadeshi campaigns between 1921 and 1922?
qh: 1921 और 1922 के बीच सार्वजनिक रूप से जलाने और स्वदेशी अभियानों के सीधे परिणाम के रूप में भारत में विदेशी कपड़ों के आयात के आंकड़ों में क्या महत्वपूर्ण बदलाव आया?
o: The value and physical imports of foreign cloth fell by half
The imports of foreign cloth doubled due to industrial factory expansions in Manchester
The import parameters remained completely constant and uniform across all ports
The trade volume dropped to absolute zero within the first week of August 1920
e: Detailed Explanation: The Swadeshi campaign against imported cloth achieved remarkable success. Massive public bonfires of foreign textiles were organized, and the picketing of shops caused the imports of foreign cloth to drop by half between 1920 and 1922.

qe: During the Non-Cooperation Movement, what functional role did the newly emerged 'Congress Volunteer Corps' play across several districts, challenging the colonial state's authority?
qh: असहयोग आंदोलन के दौरान, नवगठित 'कांग्रेस वालंटियर कॉर्प्स' (Congress Volunteer Corps) ने कई जिलों में औपनिवेशिक राज्य के अधिकार को चुनौती देते हुए क्या कार्यात्मक भूमिका निभाई थी?
o: They emerged and operated effectively as a parallel police force to maintain public order
They functioned as direct tax collection intermediaries on behalf of the local district magistrates
They were designed strictly to translate Puranic texts into European languages inside universities
They managed the logistical deployment of British military shipments across coastal ports
e: Detailed Explanation: The non-cooperation agitations weakened local administrative machinery. In many districts, the organized Congress Volunteer Corps stepped into public roles, serving effectively as a parallel police force to manage processions, enforce non-violence, and maintain public order.

qe: What macro-level constitutional or political compromise did the Indian National Congress execute under the 1916 Lucknow Pact that later drew significant criticism from secular economic nationalists?
qh: भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस ने 1916 के लखनऊ समझौते के तहत कौन सा बड़ा संवैधानिक या राजनीतिक समझौता किया था, जिसकी बाद में धर्मनिरपेक्ष आर्थिक राष्ट्रवादियों द्वारा तीखी आलोचना की गई थी?
o: The formal acceptance of the Muslim League's position on separate electorates and legislative seat weightages
The total legal abolition of the newly consolidated High Court system across presidencies
The direct physical exclusion of women from participating in national educational frameworks
The absolute requirement to pay a metabolic transit duty to support British managing agencies
e: Detailed Explanation: Under the Lucknow Pact of 1916, the Congress formally accepted the principle of separate electorates for Muslims and agreed to a fixed proportion of reserved seats in the legislatures, which critics argue institutionalized communal identities in national politics.

qe: The British Secretary of State for India, Edwin Montagu, issued a historic statement in August 1917. What did this declaration designate as the ultimate long-term goal of British policy in India?
qh: भारत के ब्रिटिश राज्य सचिव एडविन मोंटेग्यू ने अगस्त 1917 में एक ऐतिहासिक बयान जारी किया था। इस घोषणा ने भारत में ब्रिटिश नीति के अंतिम दीर्घकालिक लक्ष्य के रूप में किसे नामित किया था?
o: The progressive realization of responsible self-government for the people of India
The permanent administrative annexation of all independent princely states directly to the Crown
The complete structural termination of any Indian representation inside executive councils
The mandatory introduction of centralized non-competitive allosteric inhibitors inside all schools
e: Detailed Explanation: Pressured by the unified front of the Lucknow Pact and the Home Rule agitation, Edwin Montagu issued the August 1917 Declaration, which officially committed the British government to the gradual development of self-governing institutions and the progressive realization of responsible government in India.

qe: The Royal Commission on Decentralization (1908) made specific structural recommendations to revitalize rural local governance. Which of the following bodies did it suggest should be entrusted with more powers like petty judicial jurisdiction?
qh: रॉयल कमीशन ऑन विकेंद्रीकरण (1908) ने ग्रामीण स्थानीय शासन को पुनर्जीवित करने के लिए विशिष्ट संरचनात्मक सिफारिशें की थीं। इसने निम्नलिखित में से किस निकाय को छोटी न्यायिक अधिकार क्षेत्र जैसी अधिक शक्तियाँ सौंपने का सुझाव दिया था?
o: Village panchayats with adequate sources of income
The centralized Imperial Legislative Council nominees exclusively
The European registrar's courts room attached to Zila courts
The executive committees of the newly established Aligarh School
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1908 Commission emphasized that rural governance should be built from the grass roots. It recommended that village panchayats be revived and endowed with real administrative and petty judicial powers, along with independent sources of income.

qe: Under the judicial hierarchy organized by Lord Cornwallis between 1786 and 1793, what structural change was implemented regarding the traditional District Fauzdari Courts?
qh: 1786 और 1793 के बीच लॉर्ड कॉर्नवॉलिस द्वारा आयोजित न्यायिक पदानुक्रम के तहत, पारंपरिक जिला फौजदारी अदालतों के संबंध में कौन सा संरचनात्मक परिवर्तन लागू किया गया था?
o: They were completely abolished and replaced by provincial Circuit Courts managed by European judges
They were given supreme absolute veto power to override the decisions of the Supreme Council
They were placed under the direct operational command of the local village caste elders
Their jurisdiction was strictly limited to civil property inheritance disputes involving Europeans
e: Detailed Explanation: Lord Cornwallis reformed criminal justice by abolishing the old District Fauzdari Courts, replacing them with four provincial Circuit Courts (at Calcutta, Dacca, Murshidabad, and Patna) presided over by European judges to act as intermediate courts of appeal.

qe: What definitive change did the Government of India Act of 1858 introduce regarding the supervisory control over the administration of India after the dissolution of the East India Company?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम 1858 ने ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी के विघटन के बाद भारत के प्रशासन पर पर्यवेक्षी नियंत्रण के संबंध में क्या निश्चित परिवर्तन किया?
o: The power to govern was transferred to the British Crown, to be wielded through a Secretary of State answerable to the British Parliament
The absolute command of revenues was handed directly to the non-official Indian members of the Legislative Council
The administration was completely subordinated to a newly created Federal Court based in Allahabad
The permanent legal re-establishment of the traditional Mughal legal system under a Deputy Nizam
e: Detailed Explanation: The Act of 1858 dissolved the East India Company and transferred governance directly to the British Crown. This power was exercised through a newly created cabinet post, the Secretary of State for India, who was assisted by a 15-member council and made directly answerable to the British Parliament.

qe: The 'Cornwallis Code' of 1793 established a baseline constitutional milestone in modern Indian administrative history by firmly introducing which major concept?
qh: 1793 के 'कॉर्नवॉलिस कोड' ने किस प्रमुख अवधारणा को दृढ़ता से पेश करके आधुनिक भारतीय प्रशासनिक इतिहास में एक बुनियादी संवैधानिक मील का पत्थर स्थापित किया?
o: The principle of the sovereignty of law and the separation of revenue and justice administration
The absolute legal immunity of all colonial government officials from civil court oversight
The mandatory use of English instead of vernacular languages across all local lower subdivisions
The total structural centralization of all judicial functions under the district Collector
e: Detailed Explanation: The Cornwallis Code of 1793 was a landmark because it established the sovereignty of law and the separation of powers. It separated revenue administration from justice, divested the Collector of judicial duties, and made government officials answerable to civil courts for official actions.

qe: Under the central executive guidelines of the Government of India Act, 1919, what specific bicameral houses replaced the old unicameral Imperial Legislative Council?
qh: भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1919 के केंद्रीय कार्यकारी दिशानिर्देशों के तहत, किन विशिष्ट द्विसदनीय सदनों ने पुरानी एकसदनीय इंपीरियल लेजिस्लेटिव काउंसिल का स्थान लिया?
o: The Central Legislative Assembly (lower house) and the Council of State (upper house)
The House of Commons and the House of Lords structural branches
The British Indian Association and the All India Kisan Sabha chambers
The Sadar Diwani Adalat and the Sadar Nizamat legislative divisions
e: Detailed Explanation: The 1919 Act introduced a bicameral central legislature consisting of a lower house named the Central Legislative Assembly and an upper house named the Council of State, introducing the initial structural principle of a double-chamber parliament.

qe: The 'Treaty of Sevres', signed in May 1920 between the Allied powers and Turkey, had what direct impact on the global status of the Ottoman caliphate, deeply incensing Indian Muslims?
qh: मई 1920 में मित्र देशों की शक्तियों और तुर्की के बीच हस्ताक्षरित 'सेवर्स की संधि' (Treaty of Sevres) का ओटोमन खलीफा की वैश्विक स्थिति पर क्या सीधा प्रभाव पड़ा, जिसने भारतीय मुसलमानों को गहरा नाराज कर दिया?
o: It completely dismembered the Ottoman Empire and finalized the removal of the Khalifa from power
It successfully extended the legal control of the Khalifa over all Muslim sacred places globally
It granted absolute sovereign independence to Turkey and its neighboring Arab territories unconditionally
It forced the British Treasury to pay all administrative salaries of the Secretary of State from London funds
e: Detailed Explanation: The Treaty of Sevres completely partitioned and dismembered the Ottoman Empire, stripping the Sultan of Turkey of his territories and removing him from power. This directly targeted the religious status of the Khalifa, which incensed Muslims worldwide and drove the Khilafat agitation into its most militant mass non-cooperation phase.
